events.title: Weather tracker: Typhoon Saudel causes mass evacuations in south-east China
events.summary:
Torrential rain causes widespread damage; while north-west South Africa hit by thunderstorms and central-southern US faces oppressive heat

Typhoon Saudel brought days of torrential rain to Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian and Guangdong provinces in south-east China last week. The city of Putian, in Fujian province, recorded 416.5mm of rain in a 24-hour period between Thursday and Friday, with surrounding villages recording more than 500mm in the same period. In Fujian, authorities estimate that almost 600,000 people were evacuated from high-risk, flood-prone areas. A further 128,000 people in 53 counties were also affected across Jiangxi, with emergency evacuations affecting 9,000 people.

Flooding, landslips and infrastructure damage were reported widely in the region. More than 2,500 teachers and students were trapped in a school compound in the Zhejiang city of Wenzhou on Wednesday after extreme rainfall caused flash floods in low-lying areas. At least 1,260 people reportedly had to be rescued in Putian after a river embankment collapsed on Thursday, flattening 100 homes. On Saturday, a landslip in a village of Suichuan county, in Jiangxi province, killed three people and nine others remaining missing.

events.title: Conflicting court rulings on Missouri map threaten November’s election | First Thing

The state can’t use new congressional districts under one court order – or its old ones under another. Plus, the architects in Europe turning urban spaces into areas of climate respite

Good morning. Clashing court rulings plunged Missouri’s congressional elections into uncertainty less than two months before the November midterms that will decide which party controls a closely divided Congress.

Conservative justice Brett Kavanaugh denied the emergency request from Missouri officials to use a congressional map in November that was redrawn with Donald Trump’s support to give Republicans an edge in the midterms, but a ruling by a federal judge in Missouri temporarily prevented the state from using its old congressional maps.

Why is there legal action over the maps? The Missouri supreme court has previously ruled that the new map must go before voters to approve or reject the new districts, meaning it cannot be used in time for the November election. The president and Republicans had fumed over the decision, with Trump calling it “horrible, ridiculous, and unconstitutional”.

What are the significant changes to the map intended to favor Republicans? The revised map targeted the fifth congressional district, held by longtime Democratic representative Emanuel Cleaver of Kansas City. It reassigned portions of Kansas City to two neighboring districts represented by Republicans and stretched the remainder of Cleaver’s district far eastward into rural Republican areas.

What has the British prime minister said? Writing in the Guardian, Andy Burnham said he would “not stand by” as horrific suffering continued, and that for too long the UK had been hesitant to act “fearful of being accused of being anti-Israel”. “The measures we are taking,” he said, “are about targeting illegal settlements and increasing the pressure on the Israeli government to change course. We are not imposing sanctions on Israel as a whole.”

How has Israel reacted? Israel has ordered the closure of the British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem among retaliatory measures including entry bans on several UK lawmakers. events.summary: Centuries-old hunger stones are emerging as Europe's rivers recede. Among the most famous is the Decin hunger stone in the Elbe River with its cryptic message.

events.summary: A playful tribute to Mozart has turned into a whodunit after 210 gold-colored figures disappeared from one of Austria's busiest tourist spots. The mass theft forced organizers to end the outdoor display early.

events.title: EU waste packaging rules: Why small businesses are worried
events.summary: The EU has introduced new rules targeting packaging waste and "forever chemicals." Although the changes will be phased in slowly, some small sellers have already paused shipments due to the additional red tape.

events.title: Solar eclipse: What to look forward to
events.summary: The last solar eclipse visible from the European mainland was in 1999. Here's what to expect, and how to prepare for this rare occasion.

events.title: Making sense of Trump's executive order on US vaccinations
events.summary: President Donald Trump and his Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. have long tried to reduce the number of vaccinations available to the US public and even farm animals. The latest move in context.

events.title: How one German city plans to challenge climate extremes
events.summary: Western Europe has recorded its hottest-ever June and July, and extreme weather from drought to storms is here to stay. How can we adapt to a fundamentally altered climate? Cities like Kiel are trying new ideas.

events.title: Iran attacks US base after American strikes on tankers
events.summary: Iran said it fired ballistic missiles at a US base in Jordan early Wednesday, in retaliation for US strikes on Iranian oil tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Kharg Island, off Iran’s coast. The US said five Iranian tankers were destroyed.

events.title: 'New escalation in Yemen deeply concerning everyone in the region'
events.summary: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Jules Grange Gastinel, Researcher at the Institute for Research and Studies on the Arab and Muslim World (IREMAM). He depicts Yemen as moving from a prolonged condition of unresolved conflict into renewed regional confrontation. The relative calm established after 2022, he argues, never amounted to a durable political settlement: Yemen remains divided between rival political, financial and military institutions.

events.title: Houthis report Saudi reprisals after oil sites set ablaze in wave of strikes
events.summary: The Houthis said Saudi Arabia retaliated with strikes on Tuesday after the group targeted oil facilities, wounding dozens, as deadly fighting reignited in Yemen after a Houthi offensive towards the Red Sea's Bab al-Mandab chokepoint. The rapid round of strikes and counter-strikes follows the unravelling of a four-year truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government in July.

events.title: War in the Middle East: Iran attacks US base in Jordan, 10 US vessels
events.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Wednesday they pummelled a US military base in Jordan, vowing retaliation for American strikes on Iranian oil tankers that dragged the foes deeper into war. Tehran's bombs came after US forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday in response to Iran targeting an American warship, the second such attack in less than a week. FRANCE 24's Reza Sayah reports from Tehran, Iran.

events.title: Diplomatic row escalates as UK, France and Canada move to sanction Israeli settlements
events.summary: Britain, France and Canada said Tuesday they will ban imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, with a UK minister accusing Israel of turning a blind eye to the "ethnic cleansing" of Palestinians there. The moves prompted a furious Israel to unveil immediate counter-measures targeting Britain, as Jerusalem-based journalist Jordana Miller reports.

events.title: FRANCE 24 report reveals Russia’s war on Ukraine’s books and cultural identity
events.summary: In Ukraine, the war is not being fought solely on the battlefield. This summer, Russian strikes severely affected the publishing industry, destroying dozens of warehouses and logistics centres. Millions of books and textbooks have been lost. For many Ukrainians, these attacks are part of an effort to erase their linguistic and cultural identity, as FRANCE 24’s Yegor Terletzkyi and Emmanuelle Chaze report.

events.title: Albanian anger undiminished after 100 days of protests against Kushner project
events.summary: Police in Albania blocked protesters from reaching parliament on Tuesday at the latest rally against a luxury development linked to US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner. Dubbed the ‘flamingo revolution’ for protesters’ signs depicting the pink bird that could be harmed by the coastal development, the protests are aimed at stopping the massive project that critics say would cause environmental damage and limit public access to the coast.

events.title: How France fell in love with Céline Dion
events.summary: Two years after her dazzling performance atop the Eiffel Tower for the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris, Céline Dion is back in the French capital for a series of sold-out concerts – and fans are over the moon. Some 500,000 people are expected to attend the concerts.

events.title: US Rubio pledges to 'restore' ties with Colombia's new, Trump-friendly leader
events.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday pledged to "restore" ties with Bogota after four years of leftist rule, on day one of a three-nation tour aimed at bolstering conservative allies in Latin America. The trip to Colombia, Ecuador and Peru comes after a series of elections brought pro-US right-wing leaders to power, giving Washington an opening to tighten security and economic ties and push back against China's growing influence. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle tells us more.

events.title: Ballon d'Or: Dembélé, Kane and Mbappé among shortlisted stars
events.summary: Ousmane Dembélé, Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé are among the top contenders for the men’s Ballon d’Or. The 30 men’s and 30 women’s nominees were revealed by France Football magazine on Tuesday, with the winners to be announced at a ceremony in London on October 26.

events.title: Hormuz impasse deepens: Iran retaliates against US targets after its oil tankers destroyed
events.summary: Iran launched fresh attacks against US targets in the Middle East on Wednesday in retaliation for American strikes on Iranian oil tankers, dragging the foes deeper into war. Tehran's powerful Revolutionary Guards said Wednesday they attacked 20 US vessels trying to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for the world's oil and gas that Iran has largely controlled since the war erupted. The United States and Iran are locked in a stalemate six months into the war, with Iran maintaining a stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz and Washington pushing a campaign to choke Iran's ports and economy.

events.title: JNIM jihadists step up incursions into northern Benin
events.summary: Al Qaeda affiliate JNIM has been intensifying its activities in Benin since 2022. The country serves as a transit corridor between the areas of operation of the group, which is well established in Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso. Two nature reserves have become logistical hubs for the jihadist fighters. Benin's army is striving to hold the line.

events.title: Russian drone strike near Ukraine-Moldova border kills at least two as Ukraine targets oil terminal
events.summary: An overnight Russian drone strike at a border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova killed at least two people, Odesa's regional governor said Wednesday. Moldovan Prime Minister Vasile Tofan said that 17 drones had hit Moldovan territory in August alone as both Kyiv and Moscow ramp up long-range strikes on military and energy infrastructure.

events.title: European space sector in the spotlight as Paris hosts International Space Summit
events.summary: Paris's Grand Palais will host a two-day International Space Summit this Wednesday to promote global cooperation in the sector. A number of deals and investments for European space firms are expected to be announced as part of a wider plan to strengthen Europe's position in a field dominated by the US and China. Also in this edition: the US and Canada are locked in a tit-for-tat battle over tariffs.

events.title: Why is France so good at animation?
events.summary:
🇫🇷 🎞️ Usually associated with high fashion and culinary excellence, the French touch is prominent in another field not many know about: animation. The French animation industry is the third-largest exporter of animated content in the world, behind only the US and Japan.
 
But why is France so good at animation? FRANCE 24's Tanishk Saha explains.

events.title: OpenAI says its models solved one of math's hardest problems as researchers cry foul
events.summary: US tech giant OpenAI on Tuesday said it had solved one of the hardest problems in mathematics with an unreleased artificial intelligence model after just 88 hours – and millions of dollars' worth of computing power. But a US mathematician and a researcher at rival Anthropic allege that OpenAI only took up the problem after it had gotten wind of their own AI-assisted efforts to crack the challenge which had demanded months to craft a radically distinctive approach.

events.title: Eiffel Tower row over Hindu sect BAPS unites French politicians – but divides Indian diaspora
events.summary: France got a crash course on the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS), a Hindu sect at the heart of an Eiffel Tower strike this week. But for Indians in France who have been trying to raise awareness of far-right Hindu groups, it comes too late. As the 2027 election campaign goes into high gear, some fear the issue will be politicised by the French far right.

events.title: Rubio hails Colombia's new pro-Trump leader De la Espriella on first stop of Latin American tour

Rubio hailed the election of Colombian President Abelardo De La Espriella as part of a growing alignment with US interests across the Western Hemisphere.

events.title: Champions League: Madrid and Mbappé defeat Inter despite defensive lapses

events.title: Travellers in UK face ongoing disruption after air traffic control glitch

events.title: US bans Canadian alcohol, motorcycles and dairy products as trade spat escalates

events.title: Middle East live: Tehran targets US base in Jordan after Washington destroys five Iranian tankers
events.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard on Wednesday said it fired ballistic missiles at a base in Jordan used by the US military, attacked 10 ships, and threatened to strike tankers located off Kuwait and Bahrain in retaliation for US forces’ destruction of five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

events.title: Oil rises above $100 a barrel as Middle East conflict escalates - use our tracker to see impact on prices

events.summary: As the U.S.-Canadian relationship severely deteriorates, the White House says the import bans will go into effect in about three weeks.

events.title: Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch to retire amid clashes with Trump administration
events.summary: Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch announced he will be stepping down from his position leading the institution by the end of the year. NBC News' Andrea Mitchell has details on Bunch's accomplishments and past tensions with President Trump and his administration.

events.title: Man pleads not guilty to misdemeanor charges in Ohio fair incident involving Amy Acton
events.summary: The prosecutor said the suspect, Patrick Havas, was armed but didn’t brandish a weapon.

events.title: As Trump pushes for data centers, voters in key midterm races say they don’t want them
events.summary: An NBC News Decision Desk Poll found that 69% of respondents oppose building AI data centers in their areas, with 45% saying they “strongly oppose” the idea.

events.title: Iran attacks American warships and base after U.S. sinks five Iranian tankers
events.summary: They’re the latest tit-for-tat strikes as Washington and Tehran lurch back toward fighting during more than six months of war.

events.title: Oil hits $100 a barrel for first time in months as Middle East conflict intensifies again
events.summary: The price of oil breached the $100 threshold Wednesday for the first time in months, as new flare-ups in the United States’ war with Iran stoked fresh concern for global energy markets.

events.title: Iran increases gasoline price for its heaviest consumers as economy struggles
events.summary: TEHRAN, Iran — Iran early Tuesday introduced a higher price for its heaviest users of gasoline, state media reported, in the latest economic pinch caused by months of war.

events.title: Tracking U.S., state and county gas prices, in maps and charts
events.summary: Are gas prices declining? NBC News is tracking national, state and county prices at the pump.

events.title: New Russian attacks on Ukraine
events.summary: NBC News’ Richard Engel is on the ground in Kyiv and reports from the scene of a bloody new strike by Russia. Attacks resumed after a brief three day pause as President Trump’s envoys were in the region trying to relaunch peace efforts.

events.title: Tech company discloses first-of-its-kind A.I. cyberattack of one government against another
events.summary: Israeli cyber security firm Dream says it disclosed an A.I. hack working to compromise a government entity in Asia, thousands of miles away. NBC News’ Keir Simmons reports.

events.title: Prince George starts his first day at elite Eton College
events.summary: 13-year-old Prince George started his first day at one of Britain's most elite schools, Eton College. The future British king followed in the footsteps of Prince William and Prince Harry, who also attended Eton.

events.title: Nepal observes day of mourning after devastating floods
events.summary: Nepal observed a national day of mourning on the last day of the 13-day Hindu mourning as the government continued search operations. Priests, monks and grief-stricken residents held prayer ceremonies on the banks of the swollen Trishuli River for the more than 1,300 killed in the floods.

events.title: China hits back at U.S. claim its AI companies systematically copied American models
events.summary: In its most detailed accusation yet, the U.S. government has named six Chinese AI companies that it says copied American companies for their AI secrets.

events.title: Widespread flight delays hit major British airports
events.summary: Flights departing from two of London’s Heathrow Airport have been grounded following a “technical issue.”

events.title: Chinese hackers are running AI on stolen networks to avoid detection, Google says
events.summary: One China-linked group targets academic, medical and military AI research, the report says.

events.title: Harry and Meghan ‘surprised’ by king’s letter making clear they’re still nonworking royals
events.summary: A spokesman for the couple told NBC News that a government committee was meeting this week to discuss whether to provide security for the family now that they have moved back to the U.K.

events.title: King Charles confirms Harry and Meghan will not be working royals after U.K. return
events.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan will not be working members of Britain’s royal family now they have returned to the U.K., a letter sent on behalf of King Charles said.

events.title: U.S. envoys ‘very encouraged’ after peace talks in Moscow and Kyiv
events.summary: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner said talks were “substantive,” but neither gave details of any proposal to end the conflict.

events.title: U.S. strikes 3 Iranian oil tankers after Iran targets Navy warships, military says
events.summary: U.S. Central Command said no American personnel were harmed in the Iranian missile attacks.

events.title: Serbia accused of ‘glorifying’ convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić ahead of funeral
events.summary: BELGRADE, Serbia — The European Union’s Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos on Friday canceled an upcoming visit to candidate nation Serbia over what she described as the “glorification” of former Bosnian Serb army commander Ratko Mladić following his death.

events.title: Two trapped workers pulled alive from Nepal tunnel more than a week after deadly floods
events.summary: Two workers in Nepal were pulled out alive from a hydropower tunnel on Friday, some nine days after devastating floods swept the Himalayan region and left thousands of people missing.

events.title: Senior aides to British Trump ally Nigel Farage step down after foreign funding sting
events.summary: Britain’s populist Reform UK said two senior aides to leader Nigel Farage stepped down on Friday after an undercover investigation alleged the party had broken electoral law by arranging for a foreign donor to pay for political polling.

events.title: In Nepal, mourners hold symbolic cremation for missing loved ones
events.summary: As hopes for those still missing fade, families without the remains of their relatives are burning effigies on miniature funeral pyres.
